name: calm dark worn asphalt road with sparse aggregate, long hairline cracks, a repair patch and an oil stain, its unconnected edges crumbling into dirt with a darker broken lip and loose chunks, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road network tiles (crossroads, T-junctions, dead ends, end caps) on a dirt ground

answer.evidence: The image is a flat terrain tile sheet seen straight from above: dark asphalt road pieces with cracks, a patch and an oil stain lie on brown dirt, with crumbling dirt edges. The width profile is 256 for every row, so the sheet is a full opaque rectangle. The column scans show repeating texture bands, not a standing object's front face. No eave line, ellipse or vertical face exists. The kind is terrain, so the tiles are flat ground and have no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt is a flat blue-grey slate with only about 3 tones. Aggregate, cracks, the repair patch and the oil stain are sparse and tiny, so large asphalt areas, especially the big patch on the right, read as near-flat fill. Measured: 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference, and 8% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references. The dirt surround has mottled brown clumps in about 3 tones, which is acceptable, but the road itself, the main subject, is shallow next to the paving reference's 5-6 steps and per-stone shading. The edges have a darker broken lip tinted toward the material, not neutral black (0% neutral dark edge pixels), which is good, though the crumble is thin and mostly small speckles. The road network layout does include crossroads and dead ends. Overall the asphalt is flatter than the Beodeul standard, so this fails.
